judged_text: In onError, message is a template literal (always truthy) so the 'unable_to_add_guests' fallback in showToast(message || t('unable_to_add_guests')) is dead code, and err.data is undefined for non-TRPC errors. Users with a network/timeout failure get a toast reading 'undefined: Network request failed'-style text, and the intended generic 'Unable to add guests' message can never render; maintainers editing the fallback will find it unreachable.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the mutation `onError` builds `message` as a template literal: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal is always a truthy string, so the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is unreachable. If `err.data` is missing (e.g., non-TRPC/network error), the toast can display `undefined: ...` instead of the intended generic message, matching the finding.
